points.quote: An application is a package whose `dependencies` list the extensions it wants. ... `theia build`, from `@theia/cli`
Its `package.json` has a `theiaExtensions` array. Each entry names a frontend module, a backend module, or both
`src/browser`: frontend code that runs in the browser. `src/node`: backend code that runs in Node.
Each of those files is an InversifyJS `ContainerModule`. It binds services and contributions
The source is split by runtime: `src/browser` ... `src/node` ... `src/common` ... `src/electron-browser` and `src/electron-main`
It also has a `theia` section with `frontend.config` and `backend.config`. Those hold the application name, default preferences and similar settings.

It generates an `esbuild.mjs` config, and esbuild bundles the frontend. ... It serves the bundled frontend at localhost:3000. ... The Electron app follows the same pattern, with the backend run from the Electron main process.
